items.text: Who are you?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'm Rubuska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Are we done? This isn't funny, you know.
What's your purpose on this train?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'm going to Budapest to find a job.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Let me go.
Do you have any companions aboard?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Hmph, vampires don't team up.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: People are too scared of me.
Are you a vampire?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yeah, I'm a vampire, okay?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But so what? I didn't do anything.
She hangs her head, her whole body radiating defeat.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She doesn't bear any signs of Manus Vindictae's rituals. She may indeed be innocent.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But can't rule her out for definite yet. Best to be safe.
Semmelweis returns to the conductress's side.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I've checked her over. She's not a threat, nor is she my target.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Then this isn't any ordinary vampire you're searching for.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm not at liberty to say.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: You hear that? She says I'm not a threat!
Soon, she perks up again, a hint of color returning to her face.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But, according to regulations, dangerous creatures like vampires should be contained in such situations.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It's for the safety of all passengers. A hungry young vampire in an enclosed space like the train is always a risk.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: N-No, don't lock me up! I'm not even hungry!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: This is not a request; it's a notification. You've already admitted that you're a vampire.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Vampire, vampire, vampire! Yeah, I'm a vampire, so what?!
Her ruby eyes seem ablaze with fury.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Have I bitten anyone? Have I sucked any blood? Have I hurt even a single person?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I don't understand you people.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Always putting everyone in boxes and then treating them differently just because you put them there! It's like your brains are all square or something!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: One minute we're friends, and then the next you're tying me up. All because of these boxes you're so obsessed with.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: It's because of these boxes—these stupid labels—that this whole war started. Why I have nowhere to go?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: And now you can't wait to do the same to me. Then, fine, go ahead!
Tears begin to streak down her face.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'm a vampire! Everyone hates me! Go on! What are you waiting for?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Follow your rules! Pierce me through with a stake!

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Goodness, Rubuska, you ...
The carriage is silent for a moment. The passengers stare at the girl as if seeing her anew.
The conductress loosens the strings that bind her.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Apologies, we had to tie you up to prevent you from—

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ah-ha! The weakness is revealed.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Take this, pal!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Argh! I didn't even get a good bite in!
Resistance is futile. The conductress pins her down with ease.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You're brave.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Bold, even.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: But you're not going anywhere for now.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Let me go! Let me—

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I'll leave her to you, Investigator. The "Danube Dawn" is not a detention center. We have no obligation to take care of your travel companion.
A minor nuisance, nothing more.
If it were not for her missing teammates, the investigator wouldn't mind playing chaperone for a day.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: But, perhaps we could offer a personal favor to Ms. Semmelweis?
The stewardess, silent until now, finally speaks with a strange note of eagerness.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I'm sure I could find an empty room to take care of her, I mean, keep an eye on her.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The train will arrive at the border checkpoint later today.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: She can stay with us until then.
Semmelweis lets out a steady, meaningful breath, resigned to this course of action.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I appreciate your cooperation.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Wait, what about what I think? Where are you taking me?
Sensing the girl's unease, Aima gently takes her hand.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: You can stay in my room, Rubi.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: There's an extra sofa stuffed with goose feathers. It's ever so soft. You're welcome to have a rest there if you're tired.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Rubi?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Come to think of it, that sofa does sound tempting.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Call it "house arrest."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Allow us to escort you.
The two figures march down the narrow train corridor.
One dangles by her collar, the other nearly scraping the roof. Together, an inseparable, uncanny whole.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ach, watch it! You're pulling my hair!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'll bite you! All of you! I swear ...
If you ignore the faintest bit of noise, that is.
